conflicts.name: Iran War Theater
conflicts.description: Joint US-Israeli military operation (US: Operation Epic Fury / Israel: Operation Roaring Lion). 1000+ targets struck including military, nuclear, and leadership sites. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in Tehran strikes. Iran retaliating with missiles and drones across the region.

conflicts.name: Strait of Hormuz Crisis
conflicts.description: Iran attempting to close Strait of Hormuz. IRGC naval/air operations active. Three tankers damaged. US sank 9 Iranian warships. GPS spoofing/jamming reported. 20-30% of global oil/gas transits through this chokepoint. Brent crude spiking to $80+.

conflicts.name: Ukraine War
conflicts.description: Full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. Active frontlines in Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson oblasts. Heavy artillery, drone warfare, and trench combat.

conflicts.name: Gaza Conflict
conflicts.description: Israeli military operations in Gaza following October 7 attacks. Ground invasion, aerial bombardment. Humanitarian crisis. Regional escalation with Hezbollah.

conflicts.name: Israel-Lebanon Border
conflicts.description: Cross-border artillery and rocket fire. Targeted assassinations. High risk of full-scale escalation.

conflicts.name: Red Sea Crisis
conflicts.description: Houthi maritime campaign against commercial shipping. US/UK airstrikes on Houthi targets. Ongoing blockade attempts.

conflicts.name: Sudan Civil War
conflicts.description: Power struggle between SAF and RSF paramilitary has engulfed the entire country. RSF controls most of Darfur and Khartoum; SAF holds Port Sudan and eastern regions. World's largest displacement crisis. Famine conditions in multiple states.

conflicts.name: Myanmar Civil War
conflicts.description: Civil war following 2021 military coup. Resistance forces and ethnic armed organizations have captured significant territory. Junta losing control of border regions. Multiple coordinated offensives ongoing.

conflicts.name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
conflicts.description: 250km-long, 4km-wide buffer zone along the Military Demarcation Line established by the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement. Despite its name, one of the most heavily militarized borders in the world.

conflicts.name: Pakistan–Afghanistan Border Conflict
conflicts.description: Escalating tensions along the Pakistan–Afghanistan border. Pakistan has conducted cross-border strikes targeting TTP sanctuaries in Afghan territory, prompting border closures and diplomatic friction with the Taliban government. Long-running dispute over militant safe havens and border security.

mining.name: Oyu Tolgoi
mining.significance: World's third-largest copper-gold deposit. Underground expansion ramping up.

mining.name: Lumwana
mining.significance: One of Africa's largest copper mines. ~140kt Cu/yr. Major Zambian producer.

mining.name: Olaroz
mining.significance: Key Argentina lithium brine operation. Part of the Lithium Triangle.

mining.name: Cauchari-Olaroz
mining.significance: One of Argentina's largest lithium brine projects. Recently commenced production.

mining.name: Thacker Pass
mining.significance: Largest known lithium deposit in the US. Under development in Nevada.

mining.name: Manono
mining.significance: World's largest hard-rock lithium deposit. DRC asset under development.

mining.name: Kamoto (KOV)
mining.significance: Major DRC cobalt-copper underground mine.

mining.name: Southern China REE
mining.significance: Jiangxi/Guangdong ion-adsorption clay deposits. Key source of heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) critical for EV motors.

mining.name: Kvanefjeld
mining.significance: World-class REE + uranium deposit in Greenland. Subject to Greenland political debate.

mining.name: Morowali Industrial Park
mining.significance: Largest integrated nickel production hub globally. Drives ~50% of world's battery-grade nickel.

mining.name: Voisey's Bay
mining.significance: High-grade nickel-cobalt-copper mine in Labrador. Strategic Canadian deposit.

mining.name: Goro (Vale Nouvelle-Calédonie)
mining.significance: Major laterite nickel operation. Battery-grade nickel and cobalt production.

mining.name: Taganito
mining.significance: Key Philippine nickel laterite mine. Major Japanese nickel supply source.

mining.name: Mogalakwena
mining.significance: World's largest open-pit platinum mine. Bushveld Igneous Complex.

mining.name: Marikana / Rustenburg
mining.significance: Major Bushveld Complex platinum operations. Historically significant labor site.

mining.name: Zimplats
mining.significance: Zimbabwe's largest mining company. World's third-largest PGM producer.

mining.name: Stillwater
mining.significance: Only significant PGM mine in North America. Primary US palladium source.

mining.name: Pilbara Iron Ore (BHP)
mining.significance: BHP's Pilbara hub — world's most productive iron ore mining region. ~280Mt/yr.

mining.name: Pilbara Iron Ore (Rio Tinto)
mining.significance: Rio Tinto's Pilbara operations — 16 mines feeding 4 port facilities. ~330Mt/yr.

mining.name: Carajás
mining.significance: World's largest iron ore mine by proven reserves. Highest grade iron ore (~67% Fe).

mining.name: Sishen
mining.significance: Africa's largest iron ore mine. Major export source for European and Asian steel mills.

mining.name: Kiruna
mining.significance: Europe's largest iron ore mine. Undergoing city relocation due to mine expansion.

mining.name: McArthur River
mining.significance: World's highest-grade uranium mine. 25x average uranium ore grade. Saskatchewan, Canada.

mining.name: Cigar Lake
mining.significance: World's largest high-grade uranium deposit currently in production.

mining.name: Kazakhstan ISL Fields
mining.significance: Cluster of in-situ leaching uranium operations. Kazakhstan produces ~40% of world supply.

mining.name: Olympic Dam
mining.significance: World's largest known uranium ore body. Also produces copper, gold, silver.

mining.name: Rössing
mining.significance: One of the world's largest open-pit uranium mines. Chinese-owned since 2019.

mining.name: Husab
mining.significance: Second-largest uranium mine globally by production. 100% Chinese-owned.

mining.name: Baotou REE Processing Complex
mining.significance: World's largest rare earth processing hub. Processes ore from Bayan Obo.

mining.name: Lynas Advanced Materials Plant (LAMP)
mining.significance: Largest rare earth processing facility outside China. Processes Mt Weld ore.

mining.name: Mountain Pass Processing
mining.significance: US rare earth concentrate processing. Building downstream magnet manufacturing.

mining.name: Ganzhou Lithium Hub
mining.significance: China's major lithium chemical refining hub. Processes spodumene into battery-grade lithium.

mining.name: Kwinana Lithium Refinery
mining.significance: First lithium hydroxide refinery in Australia. Processes Greenbushes concentrate.

mining.name: Chagres Copper Smelter
mining.significance: Major Chilean copper smelter. Part of integrated Andean copper production chain.

mining.name: Nkana Copper Smelter
mining.significance: Key Zambian copper smelter and refinery on the Copperbelt.

mining.name: Aurubis Hamburg
mining.significance: Europe's largest copper smelter. Major recycled copper processor.

mining.name: Rand Refinery
mining.significance: World's largest gold refinery by cumulative output. Processes most of SA gold production.

mining.name: PAMP Refinery
mining.significance: Switzerland's leading precious metals refinery. Produces LBMA-accredited gold bars.

mining.name: Norilsk Nickel Smelter
mining.significance: World's largest nickel and palladium smelter. Also major SO2 emitter (Arctic pollution concern).

gulfInvestments.description: Largest UK container port development in 50 years. 3.5M TEU capacity on the Thames Estuary. DP World fully owns and operates.
Largest private container terminal in India at Mundra Port, Gujarat. Part of Adani Ports joint venture.
25-year concession. Primary gateway for West African trade corridor.
DP World 30-year concession. Critical Red Sea/Gulf of Aden access point and free trade zone.
DP World minority stake in Nigeria's primary container gateway through Apapa Port.
DP World 35% stake in Euromax, one of Europe's most automated deep-water terminals.
DP World manages Jeddah South, Red Sea's largest container terminal. 33% stake.
DP World-operated Caribbean transshipment hub serving Latin American trade routes.
DP World operates Chile's Lirquen port for South American logistics gateway.
DP World manages Maputo container terminal. Gateway for landlocked Southern African countries.
Flagship Abu Dhabi deepwater port. 3M+ TEU capacity. Regional container and industrial hub with automated terminal.
AD Ports 80% stake in Suez Canal economic corridor terminal. Strategic Red Sea/Mediterranean gateway.
AD Ports 70% stake in new Karachi container terminal. Pakistan's primary gateway port.
AD Ports 70% stake in Luanda container terminal. Strategic position in oil-rich Angola.
Mubadala 75% stake in Borealis, a major European plastics and chemicals producer. Manufacturing assets in Austria, Belgium, Germany, Finland.
Mubadala owns ~82% of GlobalFoundries, the world's third-largest semiconductor foundry. Fab facilities in New York, Vermont, Germany, Singapore.
Mubadala 63% stake in Cepsa, Spain's second-largest oil company with refining and pipeline assets across Spain and Portugal.
ADNOC full acquisition of Covestro (Leverkusen, Germany) — major European specialty chemicals and materials producer. Critical input supplier to automotive, construction, electronics.
ADNOC 24.9% stake in OMV (Austria). Provides access to Central European pipeline networks and refining infrastructure.
New 9.6 mtpa LNG export facility at Ruwais Industrial City. UAE's first large-scale LNG export terminal, targeting European and Asian markets.
Masdar minority stake in Hornsea offshore wind development. Part of the UK's largest offshore wind zone.
Masdar 20% stake in 630MW London Array. Previously Europe's largest offshore wind farm.
500MW wind project in Uzbekistan. Central Asia's largest wind farm at time of completion.
500MW wind farm in the Gulf of Suez corridor. Joint venture with TAQA. Part of Egypt-UAE energy cooperation.
Masdar joint venture solar assets across multiple US states. Part of broader clean energy FDI strategy.
EGA owns Guinea Alumina Corporation — a major bauxite mining operation feeding UAE aluminium smelters. Feeds 12M tonnes/year from West Africa.
PIF majority stake in Lucid Motors EV manufacturer. Plans for Lucid manufacturing facility in Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030.
PIF interest in Italy's national fixed network (NetCo) spun out from Telecom Italia. Subject to regulatory review by Italian government.
PIF's $100B electronics and technology manufacturing venture. Aims to build domestic semiconductor, consumer electronics, and EV capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
PIF-funded national cloud and hyperscale data center infrastructure as part of Vision 2030 digital economy strategy. Partnerships with Google, Microsoft, AWS.
170km linear smart city with integrated high-speed rail along the spine. PIF/Saudi Vision 2030 flagship mega-infrastructure project in Tabuk region.
World's planned largest green hydrogen-ammonia export facility. Joint venture: ACWA Power 26%, Air Products 26%, NEOM 34%.
ACWA Power stake in Benban — one of the world's largest solar parks (1.6GW total). In Aswan, Upper Egypt.
100MW utility-scale solar project in Uzbekistan's Navoi region. ACWA Power's first Central Asia project.
ACWA Power's renewable energy portfolio in South Africa under REIPPPP (Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme).
50MW Dhofar wind farm — Oman's first and the Arab world's first utility-scale wind farm.
World's largest US oil refinery (630,000 bpd). Fully Aramco-owned via Motiva Enterprises. Critical Gulf Coast downstream asset.
Saudi Aramco 30% stake in Rongsheng Petrochemical's Panjin refinery in Liaoning Province. One of China's largest private refineries.
Aramco acquired 70% of SABIC in 2020. SABIC has manufacturing in Netherlands, Germany, US, India, China — global chemicals infrastructure.
Saudi Ports Authority flagship Eastern Province gateway on the Persian Gulf. Expanding toward 7.5M TEU annual capacity.
Largest industrial port in the world by area. Services Jubail Industrial City petrochemical complex.
STC acquired 9.9% stake in Spain's Telefónica, becoming a top-3 shareholder. Gives Saudi Arabia indirect access to Telefónica's critical telecoms infrastructure across Europe and Latin America.
